walkthroughs.body_html:
William Shakespeare (1564-1616) was an English playwright and poet.

He wrote 37 plays and 154 sonnets. His works are still performed worldwide and dominate the GCSE.

Shakespeare wrote in three main genres: tragedies (Hamlet, Macbeth, King Lear), comedies (Twelfth Night, Much Ado About Nothing), and histories (Henry V, Richard III).

GCSE most commonly studies Macbeth or Romeo and Juliet.

He wrote mostly in iambic pentameter — 5 pairs of unstressed/stressed syllables per line.

Kings and nobles speak in verse. Servants and clowns speak in prose. A soliloquy lets a character share private thoughts with the audience.

mcqs.q: In which year was Shakespeare born?
Which is NOT one of Shakespeare's tragedies?
options: Hamlet
Macbeth
Twelfth Night
King Lear
Iambic pentameter is any line with ten syllables.
A line of five iambs (unstressed-stressed syllable pairs), creating a ten-syllable line with the rhythm da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
Iambic pentameter is when every line rhymes.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
Iambic pentameter is when every line rhymes.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
